```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Xu_2026_polymyxinB"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Xu_2026_polymyxinB"))$description`
* Article: [Front Pharmacol 2026;17:1859709](https://doi.org/10.3389/fphar.2026.1859709)

Xu et al. fitted a two-compartment population PK model to 92 routine
therapeutic drug monitoring concentrations of polymyxin B from 20 intensive
care patients (Table 3). No covariate was retained. The paper then used the
model to simulate two sets of 2,000 dense steady-state profiles (100 mg twice
daily, infused at 100 mg/h, sampled every 0.5 h over one 12-h interval),
filtered them, and used the results to compare maximum a posteriori Bayesian
estimation with XGBoost for predicting AUC0-12h from limited samples. The
summaries of those simulated profiles (Supplementary Tables 1 and 4) are the
validation targets of this article.

# Population

The analysis included 20 adults (17 male, 3 female; median age 53.5 years,
range 27-90) in the intensive care unit of the Third Xiangya Hospital of
Central South University, Changsha, China, treated with intravenous polymyxin
B between October 2019 and December 2020 (Table 2). Body weight was 40-120 kg
(median 64) and height 155-175 cm. Creatinine clearance ranged from 20.07 to
422.44 mL/min (median 47.38); 7 patients (35%) received continuous renal
replacement therapy. Doses were 50-200 mg twice daily (median 100 mg) at
33.33-200 mg/h (median 100 mg/h), chosen by the physician.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Xu_2026_polymyxinB")()$population`.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lcl` (CL) | log(3.05 L/h) | Table 3, CL |
| `lvc` (V1) | log(40.3 L) | Table 3, V1 |
| `lvp` (V2) | log(7.52 L) | Table 3, V2 |
| `lq` (Q) | log(29.7 L/h) | Table 3, Q |
| `etalcl` | 0.291 (variance) | Table 3, 'IIV on CL (%)' = 29.1; omega^2 reading from Methods (Scenario 1) and the check below |
| `etalvc` | 0.333 (variance) | Table 3, 'IIV on V1 (%)' = 33.3; same reading |
| no IIV on V2 and Q | -- | Results: IIV on CL and V1 only |
| `propSd` | 0.192 | Table 3, proportional error 19.2% |
| `addSd` | 0.06 mg/L | Table 3, additive error 0.06 mg/L |
| two-compartment ODE, IV infusion into `central` | n/a | Results, 'Development and evaluation of the initial PopPK model'; Methods ('intravenous PMB') |
| combined additive + proportional error | n/a | Results ('mixed additive-proportional error model') |
| covariates | none | Results: none retained from 22 screened |

# Reading of the IIV column

Table 3 prints the inter-individual variability as 'IIV on CL (%)' = 29.1
and 'IIV on V1 (%)' = 33.3. A percentage in that place is usually a
coefficient of variation, which would mean omega^2 = log(1 + 0.291^2) = 0.081
for CL. The paper itself uses another convention: Supplementary Table 2 lists
'IIV on CL (%)' = 16.1 and 'IIV on V1 (%)' = 31.9 for the model refitted to
the simulated data, and the Methods (Scenario 1) state the same estimates as
'between-subject variances (omega2) for CL and V1 ... 0.161 and 0.319'. So
the column holds omega^2 x 100.

The simulated data settle it. At steady state AUC0-12h = dose / CL, so its
distribution follows from CL alone. The paper removed simulated subjects with
AUC0-12h outside the 5th-95th percentile, so the range of the retained AUCs
is the 5th-95th percentile of the full simulation. Supplementary Table 4
gives that range as estimated by the most accurate methods (Bayesian
estimation from C6 or from C0 and C1, R^2 0.998 and 1.000 against the true
AUC).

```{r iiv-reading}
dose <- 100
cl_pop <- 3.05
auc_q <- function(omega2) dose / cl_pop * exp(qnorm(c(0.05, 0.5, 0.95)) * sqrt(omega2))
iiv_cmp <- tibble::tibble(
  source = c(
    "Model: omega^2 = 0.291 (packaged)",
    "Alternative: CV 29.1%, omega^2 = 0.081",
    "Supplementary Table 4, MAP-BE from C6",
    "Supplementary Table 4, MAP-BE from C0 and C1"
  ),
  p05 = c(auc_q(0.291)[1], auc_q(log(1 + 0.291^2))[1], 11.83, 13.87),
  p50 = c(auc_q(0.291)[2], auc_q(log(1 + 0.291^2))[2], 33.02, 33.32),
  p95 = c(auc_q(0.291)[3], auc_q(log(1 + 0.291^2))[3], 79.22, 79.53)
)
iiv_cmp |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Source" = source,
    "AUC0-12h 5th pct / min (mg*h/L)" = p05,
    "Median (mg*h/L)" = p50,
    "AUC0-12h 95th pct / max (mg*h/L)" = p95
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)

# Closed form, no simulation. The variance reading lands inside 15% of the
# published retained range at both ends; the CV reading misses the upper end
# by about a third.
pub_hi <- mean(c(79.22, 79.53))
pub_lo <- mean(c(11.83, 13.87))
stopifnot(
  abs(auc_q(0.291)[3] / pub_hi - 1) < 0.05,
  abs(auc_q(0.291)[1] / pub_lo - 1) < 0.15,
  auc_q(log(1 + 0.291^2))[3] / pub_hi < 0.7
)
```

# Virtual cohort

The paper simulated 2,000 subjects with NONMEM. Here 200 virtual patients
receive the paper's regimen, 100 mg every 12 h infused at 100 mg/h, for 50
days (100 doses), and the last interval (1188-1200 h) is sampled every 0.5 h as
in the paper. Fifty days is needed for the slowest-clearing virtual patients
(CL near 0.7 L/h, terminal half-life about 100 h) to reach steady state; after
20 days their AUC0-12h is still 4% short of dose / CL. Because the model has no covariates, a virtual patient is just
a pair of random effects. They are drawn with base R as a Latin hypercube
(one draw per 1/200 probability stratum) and passed to the model as data with
the model's own random effects switched off, so every number below is the
same on every machine and every rxode2 build. Residual error is left out: the
paper's simulation used a near-zero error (additive 0.01 mg/L, proportional
1%).

```{r cohort}
mod <- readModelDb("Xu_2026_polymyxinB")
ui <- rxode2::rxode(mod)
omega <- ui$omega

n_sub <- 200L
set.seed(2026)
lhs_eta <- function(n, variance) {
  qnorm((sample.int(n) - 0.5) / n) * sqrt(variance)
}
etas <- data.frame(
  id = seq_len(n_sub),
  etalcl = lhs_eta(n_sub, omega["etalcl", "etalcl"]),
  etalvc = lhs_eta(n_sub, omega["etalvc", "etalvc"]),
  regimen = "100 mg q12h"
)

tau <- 12
n_dose <- 100L
t_last <- (n_dose - 1L) * tau
doses <- tibble::tibble(
  time = seq(0, t_last, by = tau), amt = dose, rate = 100, evid = 1L
)
obs <- tibble::tibble(
  time = t_last + seq(0, tau, by = 0.5), amt = NA_real_, rate = NA_real_, evid = 0L
)
events <- tidyr::expand_grid(etas, dplyr::bind_rows(doses, obs)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(cmt = "central") |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
stopifnot(dplyr::n_distinct(events$id) == n_sub)
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
solve_fixed_eta <- function(model, ev, ...) {
  withCallingHandlers(
    rxode2::rxSolve(model, events = ev, omega = NA, returnType = "data.frame", ...),
    warning = function(w) {
      if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w))) {
        invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
      }
    }
  )
}
sim <- solve_fixed_eta(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), events, keep = "regimen") |>
  dplyr::mutate(tad = time - t_last)

# The random effects came from the data: clearance must equal
# exp(lcl + etalcl) for each subject.
cl_check <- sim |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, cl) |>
  dplyr::left_join(etas, by = "id")
stopifnot(
  dplyr::n_distinct(round(cl_check$cl, 8)) == n_sub,
  max(abs(cl_check$cl / (cl_pop * exp(cl_check$etalcl)) - 1)) < 1e-10
)
```

# PKNCA: steady-state exposure

```{r pknca}
conc <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, regimen, tad, Cc)
dose_df <- etas |>
  dplyr::transmute(id, regimen, tad = 0, amt = dose, duration = 1)
nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ tad | regimen + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ tad | regimen + id,
    route = "intravascular", duration = "duration"
  ),
  intervals = data.frame(
    start = 0, end = tau, auclast = TRUE, cmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE, tmax = TRUE
  )
))
nca_df <- as.data.frame(nca)

# At steady state AUC over one interval equals dose / CL. PKNCA's
# linear-up/log-down trapezoid on the paper's 0.5-h grid is checked against it.
auc_vs_exact <- nca_df |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  dplyr::left_join(cl_check |> dplyr::select(id, cl), by = "id") |>
  dplyr::mutate(rel = PPORRES / (dose / cl) - 1)
c(median_rel_pct = 100 * median(auc_vs_exact$rel), max_abs_rel_pct = 100 * max(abs(auc_vs_exact$rel)))
# Deterministic cohort. Measured largest error 0.23%, on the infusion peak.
stopifnot(nrow(auc_vs_exact) == n_sub, max(abs(auc_vs_exact$rel)) < 0.005)
```

The paper does not report an NCA of patient data. Its simulated steady-state
profiles are summarised as median concentrations at each sampling time
(Supplementary Table 1; the 1-h value is the end of infusion, i.e. Cmax, and
the 0-h value the trough) and by the estimated AUC0-12h (Supplementary Table
4; Bayesian estimation from C0 and C1, R^2 = 1.00 against the true AUC). The
paper's medians are taken after removing subjects with AUC0-12h outside the
5th-95th percentile, which leaves the median unchanged.

```{r nca-compare}
reference <- data.frame(
  regimen = "100 mg q12h",
  cmax = 4.01, # Supplementary Table 1, 1 h, modeling dataset
  cmin = 1.86, # Supplementary Table 1, 0 h
  auclast = 33.32 # Supplementary Table 4, MAP-BE from C0 and C1
)
nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca,
  reference = reference,
  by = "regimen",
  params = c("cmax", "cmin", "auclast"),
  units = c(cmax = "mg/L", cmin = "mg/L", auclast = "mg*h/L"),
  label_first_column = "NCA parameter"
)
```

# Replicate Supplementary Table 1: steady-state concentrations

Supplementary Table 1 summarises the retained simulated profiles at each
nominal time (median and range). The same AUC0-12h filter is applied here.

```{r supp-table-1}
auc_keep <- auc_vs_exact |>
  dplyr::filter(
    PPORRES >= quantile(PPORRES, 0.05),
    PPORRES <= quantile(PPORRES, 0.95)
  ) |>
  dplyr::pull(id)

published_t1 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~tad, ~pub_median, ~pub_min, ~pub_max,
  0, 1.86, 0.14, 5.78,
  0.5, 3.02, 1.25, 7.21,
  1, 4.01, 1.59, 9.27,
  2, 3.62, 1.50, 8.20,
  3, 3.37, 1.41, 7.58,
  4, 3.12, 1.33, 7.27,
  6, 2.71, 0.91, 6.52,
  8, 2.38, 0.47, 6.15,
  10, 2.09, 0.26, 5.98,
  12, 1.86, 0.15, 5.79
)
t1 <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(id %in% auc_keep, tad %in% published_t1$tad) |>
  dplyr::group_by(tad) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    sim_median = median(Cc), sim_min = min(Cc), sim_max = max(Cc),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(published_t1, by = "tad") |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (sim_median / pub_median - 1))
stopifnot(nrow(t1) == nrow(published_t1))

t1 |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    sim_range = sprintf("%.2f-%.2f", sim_min, sim_max),
    pub_range = sprintf("%.2f-%.2f", pub_min, pub_max)
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(tad, sim_median, pub_median, pct_diff, sim_range, pub_range) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Time after dose (h)" = tad,
    "Median, simulated (mg/L)" = sim_median,
    "Median, Supp. Table 1 (mg/L)" = pub_median,
    "Difference (%)" = pct_diff,
    "Range, simulated" = sim_range,
    "Range, Supp. Table 1" = pub_range
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)

# Deterministic cohort (base-R Latin hypercube passed as data), so the
# medians do not move between machines; the largest difference is at the
# troughs.
c(median_abs_pct = median(abs(t1$pct_diff)), max_abs_pct = max(abs(t1$pct_diff)))
stopifnot(
  median(abs(t1$pct_diff)) < 5,
  max(abs(t1$pct_diff)) < 10
)
```

The simulated ranges come from `r length(auc_keep)` retained subjects against
the paper's 1,579, so they are expected to be somewhat narrower. Re-solving
the same cohort with the CV reading of the IIV column (each random effect
rescaled to omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)) shows the concentration-scale
counterpart of the AUC check above:

```{r cv-reading}
cv_scale <- c(
  etalcl = sqrt(log(1 + 0.291^2) / 0.291),
  etalvc = sqrt(log(1 + 0.333^2) / 0.333)
)
events_cv <- events |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    etalcl = etalcl * cv_scale[["etalcl"]],
    etalvc = etalvc * cv_scale[["etalvc"]]
  )
sim_cv <- solve_fixed_eta(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), events_cv) |>
  dplyr::mutate(tad = time - t_last)
auc_cv <- sim_cv |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, cl) |>
  dplyr::mutate(auc = dose / cl)
keep_cv <- auc_cv$id[auc_cv$auc >= quantile(auc_cv$auc, 0.05) &
  auc_cv$auc <= quantile(auc_cv$auc, 0.95)]
trough_range <- function(s, keep) range(s$Cc[s$id %in% keep & s$tad == 0])
trough_cmp <- rbind(
  "omega^2 reading (packaged)" = trough_range(sim, auc_keep),
  "CV reading" = trough_range(sim_cv, keep_cv),
  "Supplementary Table 1" = c(0.14, 5.78)
)
colnames(trough_cmp) <- c("Lowest trough (mg/L)", "Highest trough (mg/L)")
knitr::kable(trough_cmp, digits = 2)
```

```{r profile-plot, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4}
sim |>
  dplyr::filter(id %in% auc_keep) |>
  dplyr::group_by(tad) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), Q50 = median(Cc), Q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(tad, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = published_t1, aes(tad, pub_median), colour = "red") +
  labs(
    x = "Time after start of infusion at steady state (h)",
    y = "Polymyxin B Cc (mg/L)",
    caption = paste(
      "Line and band: simulated median and 5th-95th percentiles (no residual error).",
      "Red points: Supplementary Table 1 medians of Xu 2026.",
      sep = "\n"
    )
  )
```

# Exposure against the dosing target

The paper's online dosing tool aims at AUCss,0-24h of 50-100 mg*h/L. For the
simulated 100 mg twice-daily regimen (all 200 subjects, before the AUC
filter):

```{r target}
auc24 <- 2 * auc_vs_exact$PPORRES
c(
  below_50_pct = 100 * mean(auc24 < 50),
  in_50_100_pct = 100 * mean(auc24 >= 50 & auc24 <= 100),
  above_100_pct = 100 * mean(auc24 > 100)
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **IIV column read as omega^2 x 100.** Table 3 prints 'IIV on CL (%)' and
  'IIV on V1 (%)'. The Methods restate the same column of Supplementary Table
  2 as variances, and the AUC and concentration ranges of the paper's own
  simulated data agree with the variance reading and not with a coefficient
  of variation (see above). The model therefore uses omega^2 = 0.291 (CL) and
  0.333 (V1), i.e. about 58% and 62% CV.
- **Residual error as standard deviations.** Table 3 gives the proportional
  error as 19.2% and the additive error as 0.06 mg/L. The Methods write the
  residual model of the refitted model as
  sigma = sqrt(0.01^2 + (0.01 * Cpred)^2) for the Supplementary Table 2 values
  1% and 0.01 mg/L, so both rows are standard deviations; they are encoded as
  `propSd = 0.192` and `addSd = 0.06` in a combined (additive variance plus
  proportional variance) error model.
- **Analyte.** Polymyxin B1 and B2 were both assayed. The paper reports a
  single polymyxin B (PMB) concentration without stating how the components
  were combined; the model describes that single concentration, in mg/L.
- **Models fitted to simulated data are not packaged.** The paper also fitted
  a two-compartment model to the dense simulated profiles (Supplementary
  Table 2: CL 3.04 L/h, V1 40.6 L, V2 7.41 L, Q 28.8 L/h, omega^2 0.161 and
  0.319) and four one-compartment models to sparse subsets of them
  (Supplementary Table 5). They describe the simulated data set used to train
  the Bayesian estimators, not a patient population, and are not separate
  models of polymyxin B; only the Table 3 patient model is packaged. The
  XGBoost models (Supplementary Tables 3 and 6) are not pharmacometric models.
- **Simulation scale and noise.** The paper simulated 2,000 subjects with
  1% random noise on the sampling times and a near-zero residual error, then
  applied four filters. This article uses 200 subjects, nominal times, no
  residual error and only the AUC0-12h 5th-95th percentile filter, which is
  the one that shapes the distribution; the other three removed 245 of 2,000
  subjects for trough timing or negative values, which depend on the
  time noise and residual error.
- No erratum or correction notice for this article was found (Europe PMC
  search, 2026-11-14).
